title: PromptLens
author: Kynous
selftext:
I'm Kris from SoulFlux Studios. Explaining UI bugs, layout issues, or visual changes over text or to an AI assistant usually takes too many steps...taking a screenshot, saving it somewhere, opening an editor, drawing boxes, and then typing out a separate paragraph trying to explain which box means what. So I built a separate tool in Rust called PromptLens just for that.



This short 2-minute video only covers the basics, so here is a rundown of what it actually does:

**Screen and window capture**  
Grab a region, a single window, a scrolling window capture, or just paste an image straight from your clipboard.

**Connected callouts and notes**  
Draw shapes, arrows, or numbered callouts on the canvas and type your notes directly into the side panel so each comment stays tied to what you pointed at.

**Voice memos**  
Press Ctrl+R to record a quick audio note with your chosen microphone when talking through feedback is faster than typing.

**Crop and strip slicing**  
Crop the image, or press V or H to slice out vertical or horizontal strips in the middle of a screenshot (with full undo and redo if you change your mind).

**Blackout and pixelation**  
Hide sensitive info before sharing.

**Editable Smart PNGs**  
Save your work as a normal PNG that keeps your shapes, notes, and voice memos tucked inside the file, so you can reopen it later and keep making adjustments.

**One-step sharing for teammates or AI**  
Copy the marked-up image and structured notes together to your clipboard, copy just a flat image, or export everything to a Markdown document that includes the for every shape and callout so an AI assistant knows the exact spot on screen you are talking about.**exact pixel-accurate coordinates.**

**Custom settings and portable mode**  
Pick your output folders, microphone, capture shortcuts, and tray behavior, or run it from a portable folder where all your settings and captures stay together.

It's completely free to use (with optional tips on [itch.io](http://itch.io) if it saves you time): [https://kynous.itch.io/promptlens](https://kynous.itch.io/promptlens)



It is only available on Windows right now, as I haven't had a chance to fully test it on Linux yet.
